We need to apply template 1679747 to the molecule (initial_molecule SMILES: C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2). The template is given in mapped_rxn: 'O=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][c:6]([O:7][CH3:8])[cH:9][cH:10]1)[c:11]1[cH:12][cH:13][c:14]([O:15][CH3:16])[cH:17][cH:18]1.[Li][CH2:1][Si](C)(C)C>>[CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][c:6]([O:7][CH3:8])[cH:9][cH:10]1)[c:11]1[cH:12][cH:13][c:14]([O:15][CH3:16])[cH:17][cH:18]1'

So forward reaction: a carbonyl (O= C) attached to aromatic rings plus LiCH2Si(C)(C)C (a silyl carbanion) gives product: CH2= C( aromatic ) aromatic (i.e., a stilbene with methoxy groups). The template is a retrosynthetic transformation: break the double bond to form a carbonyl and a silyl carbanion? Actually retrosynthetic: product is alkene (C=C) attached to two aromatic rings each with OMe substituents. The template likely corresponds to a Wittig-type reaction: a silyl carbanion (maybe a silyl-stabilized carbanion) reacting with a carbonyl to give alkene. So applying retrosynthetic template to target molecule should give precursors: a carbonyl (aryl-CO-aryl?) and LiCH2Si(C)(C)C (the ylide). The template ID 1679747.

We need to use apply_template tool with molecule_smiles = initial_molecule and template_id = "1679747". Let's call apply_template.
